correctness.rationale: For each of all 256^3 rule triples, a four-vertex labeled de Bruijn graph recognizes every finite aligned output block, and reachability in its 16-state subset automaton exactly characterizes global surjectivity via compactness. Two independently written full C++17 enumerators, one grouping three edges and one constructing directly from each of 32 five-bit windows, agree on the complete histogram (12888,7476480,8825488,453144,9216), all surjective-constituent masks (0,0,0,928,0,928,928,10104) and sharp four-block witnesses. This is exhaustive finite proof rather than extrapolation.

value.rationale: Spatial period three is the first three-constituent heterogeneity class of elementary rules. The classification uncovers a new qualitative obstruction: a surjective global system cannot contain two homogeneously nonsurjective constituent rules, but can contain exactly one, with precisely 2784 cases. The sharp four-block bound is a uniform finite diagnostic for every nonsurjective triple. These are natural, exact structural properties rather than arbitrary parameter slices or sample computations.
